findings.title: [P2] Detect content changes when checking probe write isolation
findings.body: The probe runs arbitrary commands with access to the main checkout, but the write check compares only Git status text. If a tracked file is already modified before the probe, changing its contents again leaves the same porcelain entry; changes inside an already reported ignored directory can likewise remain invisible. A probe can therefore alter main-tree application code and still receive exit 0. Record and compare file contents and HEAD, or enforce filesystem write isolation for the probe.
findings.description: The probe's Git status comparison can miss content changes to already modified tracked files and changes within already reported ignored directories, allowing writes to the main checkout to go undetected.
findings.failure_mode: The probe's Git status comparison can miss content changes to already modified tracked files and changes within already reported ignored directories, allowing writes to the main checkout to go undetec

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-guard.sh --close-consumed returns exit 0 in an unattended context without naming or checking a map; chart-ticket.sh op_close then performs the destructive close with no Status or frontier check, so the two together let an unattended run close any charting map.
findings.description: The only operation /chart allows unattended is `close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle>` on a handed-off map. op_close enforces the interactive context only on the --reason branch. On the --consumed-by branch it never reads `doc_field Status`, never checks that the frontier is empty, and accepts any token matching the cycle-id regex. An autonomous run (LOA_UNATTENDED=1, run mode) can therefore call `chart-ticket.sh close --map <slug> --consumed-by x` on a map still in `charting`, which rejects every open ledger row, closes every question bead and the epic, and marks the map closed. That defeats the interactive-only invariant the guard exists to protect and irreversibly discards operator decisions still in flight.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended agent (or prompt-injected session) closes an in-progress map, rejecting all open decision rows and closing all beads under cover of the sanctioned --consumed-by exception.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, when CONSUMED is set require `doc_field Status == handed-off` (and no open rows) before any write; otherwise fall through to the interactive context check. Make chart-guard.sh --close-consumed take --map and perform the same Status check. Validate --consumed-by against the real cycle ledger (grimoires/loa/ledger.json) rather than a bare regex.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff registers chart-researcher as write_capable: true and the diff version of .claude/agents/chart-researcher.md grants the Write tool; op_research_end in chart-ticket.sh is the only scope check for what that subagent did, and it is defeatable from inside the writable directory.
findings.description: The diff grants chart-researcher a Write tool and marks it write_capable (the P0 full-file snapshot of chart-researcher.md contradicts this and shows no Write; the two must be reconciled, and agent-types.yaml still says write_capable: true). With Write, the subagent that reads untrusted web pages can write under grimoires/loa/research/, and op_research_end exempts that whole directory from its `bad` filter. The dispatch marker `.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch` lives in that same directory and is both the comm baseline and the `-newer` reference for .run/.beads. A prompt-injected subagent can overwrite the marker with the current `git status` output (defeating comm) and thereby make it newer than every .run/.beads file (defeating -newer). Writes into `.git/` (hooks, config) are also invisible to `git status`, so a hook payload would survive the check and run on the next git command.
findings.failure_mode: Web-sourced prompt injection drives the researcher to write arbitrary files (other reports, .git/hooks, .run state) and then rewrite the dispatch marker so research-end reports a clean scope check.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop Write from the agent (match the full-file version: return the report as the final message, session saves it) and set write_capable: false. Store the dispatch marker outside the agent-writable tree (e.g. mktemp under $ROOT/.run or $TMPDIR) and record its sha256; compare content hashes of tracked files, not just porcelain lines; explicitly fail if anything under .git/ changed.

findings.description: The probe helper's containment claim is that the main tree is unchanged if `git status --porcelain` is identical before and after. That misses three escape routes. (1) The throwaway worktree shares `$MAIN/.git` (config, hooks, refs); `git config core.hooksPath /tmp/x` or writing `$MAIN/.git/hooks/post-checkout` from the probe changes nothing git status reports, yet executes on the operator's next git command. (2) A file already listed as modified before the probe (` M path`) can be rewritten with different content and the status line is unchanged. (3) Anything outside the repository (~/.bashrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.claude/) is out of scope entirely. The helper also never verifies that --ticket is a `question` bead carrying `decision:unblock`, so it is a general arbitrary-command runner with a misleading clean verdict.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe (agent-chosen or prompt-injected) plants a git hook or hooksPath via the shared .git directory and the helper exits 0, giving persistent code execution on the next git invocation.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot and compare sha256 of `$MAIN/.git/config`, `$MAIN/.git/hooks/*` and of every pre-modified tracked file; run the probe with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`; use `git worktree add` on a separate clone (`git clone --shared`) so .git is not shared; verify via `br show --json` that the ticket is type question with label decision:unblock before running anything.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 hook now lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through when grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml holds a `decided` row whose last to=decided transition `by` starts with `operator:`. That ledger is a plain tracked YAML file the agent can edit with its normal file tools, and `operator:` is an unauthenticated string prefix. An agent can append a forged decided row for a spike it wants gone and then force-delete the unmerged branch, which is exactly the data loss FR-1.1 exists to prevent. No check that the branch was pushed to origin (the stated design: spikes are pushed, never merged) is made.
findings.failure_mode: Forged ledger row disables the destructive-bash fence for spike branches; unmerged prototype work is deleted locally without a remote copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `git rev-parse origin/spike/<slug>` to exist and equal the local branch head before exempting; or verify ledger integrity (hash chain / signature maintained by dec-write-lib.sh) rather than trusting a text prefix. Keep the block if either check fails.

findings.description:
section_append passes operator/agent text into awk via `-v line="$2"`. awk processes backslash escapes in -v assignments, so `
`, `	` and `"` survive san1 (which strips control bytes but not backslashes) and expand into real newlines inside the tracked map doc. A `--line`, `--name`, or `--why` value such as `ok
## Closed` or `ok
- forged bullet` forges headings and bullets in grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md. That doc is parsed by section_bullets for the handoff gate, by `grep -qE '^## Closed$'` in op_close, and is inlined unsanitized (only the research reports go through the L6 sanitizer) into the priority-1 hand-off snapshot that /plan-and-analyze treats as settled context.
findings.failure_mode: Newline injection through awk -v rewrites map-doc structure and smuggles instruction-like lines into priority-1 planning context.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass text to awk via ENVIRON (`line="$2" awk '... ENVIRON["line"] ...'`) or via a here-string on a separate fd instead of -v; additionally strip or reject backslashes in san1 and reject any value containing `## ` or a leading `- ` for fields that become bullets.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-frontier.sh reads the bead type as `.issue_type // .type`, acknowledging br may emit either field; get-ready-work.sh filters only `.issue_type`, so the two scripts disagree on the field that enforces the question-bead exclusion.
findings.description: The build-path invariant that `question` beads never become sprint work rests on `map(select((.issue_type // "") != "question"))`. If br emits the type as `type` (the frontier script explicitly handles that shape), `.issue_type // ""` is empty, the predicate is true, and every decision ticket flows into /implement and /run as ready work. The header claims the filter is robust regardless of labels, but it is brittle on field name. No secondary filter (e.g. `decision:` label or parent epic labelled map) backs it up.
findings.failure_mode: Decision tickets silently enter autonomous build selection and get implemented or closed by the agent, bypassing the operator-only decision flow.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same `(.issue_type // .type // "")` expression as chart-frontier.sh, and additionally drop any bead carrying a `decision:` label. Add a bats case with the `type` field shape.

findings.description: SP-1 only fires when the literal `spike/` appears in the command. Equivalent flows the header does not list: `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD` (second segment has no spike ref), `b=spike/x; git merge "$b"` (variable expansion), `git merge refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` after a remote-head trick, and `git worktree add` on a spike ref followed by `cp`. These are consistent with the stated fence-not-boundary posture, but FETCH_HEAD is the most common merge idiom and should be covered or documented.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content reaches a working branch through a two-step fetch/merge the pattern never inspects.
findings.suggested_fix: Block `git merge|rebase|cherry-pick FETCH_HEAD` when any prior segment of the same command fetched a spike/ ref, and have run-mode-ice.sh refuse merges whose merge-base commit is reachable only from spike/* refs (offline `git branch --contains`).
